title: The Apex Predator: Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach

scenes.headline: Most Powerful Boxster
scenes.narration: 493 horsepower and a 9,000 RPM redline make this the most powerful Boxster ever produced.

scenes.headline: Production Year
scenes.narration: The 2025 Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach uses Porsche’s 992 GT3-sourced 4.0-liter flat-six, creating an open-top masterpiece that stays lighter than its fixed-roof sibling.
The carbon fiber hood with its functional air vents showcases an aggressive design aimed at ultimate performance.
A prominent rear wing design aids downforce, critical at high speeds on the track.
The rear's aerodynamic features are engineered for stability, adding to the Spyder's race-ready lineage.

scenes.headline: Torque
scenes.narration: With 331 lb-ft of torque, the flat-six engine provides a thrilling driving experience.

scenes.headline: Carbon Fiber Accents
scenes.narration: Inside, carbon fiber accents are used strategically to reduce weight while enhancing aesthetics.

scenes.headline: Limited Run Prices
scenes.narration: Launched at $217,545, the 718 Spyder RS's limited production retains noteworthy market value.

scenes.headline: Rival Comparison
scenes.narration: Facing the 2025 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 with 800 horsepower, the Porsche’s agility and lighter frame provide a contrasting driving thrill.
So, does the ultimate Boxster redefine your idea of open-top performance, or is raw power more your style?

script: 493 horsepower and a 9,000 RPM redline make this the most powerful Boxster ever produced. The 2025 Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach uses Porsche’s 992 GT3-sourced 4.0-liter flat-six, creating an open-top masterpiece that stays lighter than its fixed-roof sibling. The carbon fiber hood with its functional air vents showcases an aggressive design aimed at ultimate performance. A prominent rear wing design aids downforce, critical at high speeds on the track. The rear's aerodynamic features are engineered for stability, adding to the Spyder's race-ready lineage. With 331 lb-ft of torque, the flat-six engine provides a thrilling driving experience. Inside, carbon fiber accents are used strategically to reduce weight while enhancing aesthetics. Launched at $217,545, the 718 Spyder RS's limited production retains noteworthy market value. Facing the 2025 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 with 800 horsepower, the Porsche’s agility and lighter frame provide a contrasting driving thrill. So, does the ultimate Boxster redefine your idea of open-top performance, or is raw power more your style?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2025 Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach, finished in Guards Red with a black soft top and a black interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 600 miles. This 718 Spyder RS is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this 718 Spyder RS cost $217,545 new, including over $41,000 in options. A partial list of notable equipment includes the Weissach package, 20-inch forged magnesium wheels, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB), LED headlights with Porsche Dynamic Light System (PDLS), a Spyder RS soft top, leather and Race-Tex upholstery, power-adjustable heated Adaptive Sport Plus seats, a Guards Red stopwatch dial, a Bose surround sound system, and illuminated carbon-fiber door sill guards. The selling dealer reports no notable modifications. The 718 Spyder RS stands out as the most powerful and extreme Boxster ever made. The main bones are shared with the Cayman GT4 RS, including a 992 GT3-sourced 4.0-liter flat-6 engine and a short-ratio dual-clutch transmission. To top it off, the 718 Boxster Spyder RS is lighter than its fixed-roof sibling and features a bespoke chassis setup, resulting in one of the greatest open-top sports cars of the modern era. Power comes from a 4.0-liter flat-6, rated at about 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.
